alignments.note: Rule 31: the article precedes the noun it governs across an interposed prepositional phrase, so it takes the discontinuous 'the ... which' and the noun stands bare.

Rule 67: the supplied frame 'according to the will of' rides undivided with the expressed preposition, no article standing to carry it and theon being anarthrous; rule 11 keeps the ASV's italics from making it 'added'. Rule 67 leaves the head of a proper preposition's frame divided in the corpus, and this follows the reading this book's neighbours took - 1PE.1.14's en -> 'in *the time of*' headed on 'in', with 2PE.2.2 and 2PE.3.12 - and 'according to' is already the corpus's ordinary complete gloss of kata. A head on the supplied 'will' is the competing reading.

alignments.note: The compound verb is rendered by the English phrasal idiom 'lording it over'; the pleonastic 'it' and the particle 'over' are helpers on the verb under rule 7, no Greek preposition being expressed for rule 36 to place them on. 2CO.11.19's 'ye bear with the foolish' is the same shape - phrasal verb, articular genitive complement - and keeps the particle on the verb, as PHP.3.2 and JUD.1.21 do; the corpus renders no article 'over'.

Article realized as 'the' under rule 19; the governed genitive carries no case preposition of its own here, 'over' belonging to the verb's idiom, so the article takes a bare 'the' as at 2CO.11.19, JUD.1.21 and TIT.2.13. Rule 21 is not reached: 'over' is not an English case marker for a genitive.

Medium because rule 91's operational test cannot settle it: the corpus spends neither word on kler-, whose one unit is JHN.19.24 -> 'lots', so 'allotted' remains defensible under rule 66.

Rule 62 answers the objection that rule 53 names only prepositional, adjectival and adverbial predicates: the test does not turn on the verb being a copula, and an expressed subject does not change it. 2PE.3.18 is the unhedged twin.
